explanation: Compared against Green's '100 open problems', Problem 70: fix k, ℓ; given n ≥ n₀(k,ℓ) points in ℝ², must either some k lie on a line or some ℓ be mutually visible (segments joining them contain no other point of the set)? The Lean statement: ∀ k ℓ ∃ n₀ ∀ finite P ⊆ ℝ×ℝ with |P| ≥ n₀, HasCollinear k P (k points of P collinear) ∨ HasMutuallyVisible ℓ P (ℓ points pairwise visible, with Visible meaning the open segment contains no point of P). 'Mutually visible' as pairwise visibility is the standard reading (Kára–Pór–Wood's big-line-big-clique conjecture). Degenerate small k are trivially true and harmless. Faithful.
